teams.blurb: I like my team. I usually rank myself pretty low in initial power rankings, but I think I did a good enough job this year to warrant a high ranking. The team is projected to score the 3rd most points in Week 1, but my opponent is projected to produce the most, so it’ll be a potential shootout [[img:ethan_01]]. I think one of Jaxson Dart or Bo Nix will have a top 7 QB season, but we’ll have to wait and see which one, hopefully not neither. Ashton Jeanty’s injury does concern me a little bit, but if he’s good to go, then this may be the best RB duo in the league. As you can probably guess, my hopes for Omarion Hampton are sky high, with the addition of Mike McDaniel and an O-Line that’s expected to be the most improved out of any in the league [[img:ethan_02]]. The WR core of Zay Flowers, Jaylen Waddle, and Parker Washington doesn’t strike fear into ANYONE’s heart, but I think the upside is there for each and every one of them to produce, although Parker Washington may not live up to the hype he’s getting. I also have high hopes for De’Zhaun Stribling; he could be a nothing burger, but I don’t trust Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel to remain healthy the entire season, and San Francisco likes to throw the ball. Will the team that has made the playoffs every season make it once again, or will this be the year everything comes crashing down [[img:ethan_03]]?

teams.synopsis: This was pretty simple for me.
teams.blurb: This was pretty simple for me. Charlie is projected to score the 2nd most points in Week 1; he has the 5th easiest projected strength of schedule; historically, he is one of the best drafters in league history, and I really liked his draft [[img:charlie_01]][[img:charlie_02]][[img:charlie_03]]. At QB11, Trevor Lawrence is absolute value; he also took the Drake London fall at the 2-3 turn, which is incredible value as well. The WR duo of London and George Pickens is top five minimum; Terry McLaurin is a fine FLEX too, but Charlie also drafted Romeo Doubs as some WR depth, which I think could be a great bet down the line. Reuniting Jahmyr Gibbs and David Montgomery is also cool to see, and even if Montgomery doesn’t give Charlie what he expects out of him, he still has Rico Dowdle and Chuba Hubbard off the bench, which either could be viable depending on the matchup and how their backfield mates fare throughout the season. If I were Charlie, I think my only cause for concern with this roster as currently constructed would be the TE; Dalton Kincaid hasn’t been consistent or healthy throughout his career so far, but if he finds it this season or Charlie fills the position with a sleeper, then I think the team has a good chance to make it back to the championship in 2026.

teams.synopsis: At first glance, I can see people dismissing this team, but let’s look deeper.
teams.blurb: At first glance, I can see people dismissing this team, but let’s look deeper. Sure, the QB duo of Matthew Stafford and Jordan Love doesn’t make me feel anything special, and Juwan Johnson and Dalton Schultz as the team’s TEs could be perceived as underwhelming, but let’s look at the WRs and RBs for a second. Javonte Williams has zero competition in Dallas with a passing attack that some might call the best in the league; he was 6th out of all RBs last season with 11 rushing TDs. I could see him pushing even higher this year [[img:aidan_01]]. This offseason, the Jaguars let Travis Etienne Jr. walk, and they only brought in Chris Rodriguez Jr.; that means that there are 260 carries, 52 targets, and 13 touchdowns that just walked out the door, and someone has to take them on. Even if the volume doesn’t get replaced by RBs only, the guy to take most of the load is Bhayshul Tuten. I won’t go too in-depth with the WRs because I think we all know what Chris Olave and Ja’Marr Chase are capable of. Jameson Williams is interesting because I wonder if he’ll get the volume he got last year. If Sam LaPorta is healthy, then I doubt it, but you never know. Nevertheless, the bench has a few upside players that could make Aidan a prime trade candidate down the line, or even just give him a good FLEX option no matter the week. Out of the 85 teams since 2020, Aidan’s 2025 team, which led him to last place, had the 6th lowest PPG [[img:aidan_02]]. I’m expecting a bounce-back season.

teams.synopsis: Going to need that name changed at some point.
teams.blurb: Going to need that name changed at some point. When Carmine first asked me what I thought about his team, I drunkenly replied that I thought it was a borderline playoff team, like that 7-10 rank range, but after sitting on it I’ve changed my opinion. I don’t love the idea of paying up for any QB not named Josh Allen, but Drake Maye was the QB2 last year and now gets an improved WR core that has A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs, so I can see yet another top five season for him. Bijan Robinson is one of the safest picks this year, while Breece Hall could finish as a top 12 RB if the Jets offense is legit, making this duo one of the best in the league. Nico Collins and DJ Moore wouldn’t be picks that I make, but they’re both the top targets in their offenses, so why not? TE and FLEX are still questionable to me, but the avenues for both Mark Andrews and Wan’Dale Robinson to be viable options at each position are very reasonable. No more Isaiah Likely to be competition for Andrews, and Wan’Dale could be the safety blanket in the slot to Cam Ward like he was to Jaxson Dart last season. Also, who am I to question Carmine’s drafting abilities? He currently ranks as the best drafter in league history, in his own tier with Charlie Gorman [[img:carmine_01]]. After a poor performance in 2024 and an early exit in 2025, I think there’s a good chance the manager with the 3rd highest win percentage of all-time returns to his prime form to compete for another championship in 2026 [[img:carmine_02]].

teams.synopsis: To round out the bottom half of the Week 1 rankings for 2026, we have Ben Castaldo, who had his best regular season record of all time in 2025, although it ended in disappointment with a Quarterfinal loss to Charlie Gorman .
teams.blurb: To round out the bottom half of the Week 1 rankings for 2026, we have Ben Castaldo, who had his best regular season record of all time in 2025, although it ended in disappointment with a Quarterfinal loss to Charlie Gorman [[img:ben_01]]. Looking to reach the playoffs once again and capture that 2nd championship he’s been chasing since 2021, Ben left the draft with little to no holes in his starting lineup, hence why he’s projected to produce the 4th most points in Week 1 [[img:ben_02]]. Kenneth Walker III and Travis Etienne Jr. find themselves on new teams this season with prime opportunities to finish as top players at the position or at least top twelve. Lamar Jackson is set up to bounce back to his top two QB level with a new coaching staff and no health concerns leading up to Week 1. Kyle Pitts Sr. should have a strong season with either QB at the helm of the Falcons offense, but my main concerns with Ben’s team are the WRs and specifically the consistency from those WRs. CeeDee Lamb is a great talent, but will he and George Pickens be able to share the stage? DK Metcalf produced high-end WR2 numbers occasionally last year, but will the introduction of Michael Pittman Jr. to that Steelers offense disrupt that and make him more inconsistent? Will Jakobi Meyers be consistent enough in the crowded Jacksonville offense to be a reliable FLEX option? I think 8th is the perfect spot for this team before the season begins, but if Ben’s history has taught us anything, it’s that the team will either be moving up or down the rankings before long.

This should be a no-brainer. Deniz comes into this season as the 2nd worst drafter in league history, according to my surplus value draft metric that attempts to capture drafting ability [[img:deniz_01]]. Add to that historical lack of success the fact that Josh Jacobs is now out indefinitely, forcing Deniz to play the Tampa Bay backfield as his RB1 and RB2 and Xavier Worthy as his FLEX, which is not ideal. However, Tampa Bay is expected to have a top five O-Line this season, much improved from their below average O-Line in 2025, and a new offensive play caller with a history of running the ball at the goal line above league average; I think there’s potential in that backfield, but we’ll have to wait and see [[img:deniz_02]]. I’m one of Trey McBride’s biggest fans, but I do expect a little bit of a step back from where he was producing last year. Carnell Tate is also a little too much of a question mark for this team’s roster construction in my opinion, but if he can have a standout rookie season like we’ve seen from players in recent years, then Deniz’s WR room should be formidable. Nothing else really stands out to me on this team’s roster; Deniz is an early top candidate for trades.

Will this be his year? We’ve been hearing the same thing every year since his 2020 championship loss: how this is going to be the year that The Minutemen get over the hump. Brandon has the 4th best regular season record all-time, making the playoffs every year except for 2025; in addition to being 4th all-time in PPG, he’s still the only manager within the top five best records all-time to not have a single championship [[img:brandon_01]]. Personally, he shocked me by taking Jonathan Taylor with the 4th overall pick, but when you have the opportunity to get your guy, you do it. There are question marks surrounding his one and only TE, T.J. Hockenson, and whether Jalen Hurts will be able to maintain his high-end QB1 status even without A.J. Brown in Philadelphia, but I think the WR duo of Rashee Rice and Rome Odunze has the potential to be a top duo in the league. Some may also question whether Kyren Williams will maintain a hold on that backfield, same for Jaylen Warren, and I think many have seen the Jonathan Taylor stat of him averaging around 22 PPG in Colts wins but only around 12 PPG in Colts losses, so it appears a bet on Taylor is a bet on Indianapolis. Brandon “reached” on every one of his picks aside from Jaylen Warren, according to ESPN’s ADP at the time of our draft, so I expect him to be very confident in his guys and his chances to get over the hump in 2026 [[img:brandon_02]]. Let’s Go, Brandon.

teams.synopsis: It’s been a rough Preach Fantasy career for Quin, aside from his 2024 campaign, which ironically ended with a stretch from Week 14 to Round 2 that is rated as the hardest three-week stretch in all of league history .
teams.blurb: It’s been a rough Preach Fantasy career for Quin, aside from his 2024 campaign, which ironically ended with a stretch from Week 14 to Round 2 that is rated as the hardest three-week stretch in all of league history [[img:quin_01]]. A couple of Quin’s picks were great in my opinion, specifically the WR duo of Malik Nabers and DeVonta Smith; there’s a legitimate chance that both of them finish as top five WRs in my opinion, and Quin got them as the WR8 and WR17, respectively. However, I didn’t love the Quinshon Judkins pick; he could make me eat my words, but Cleveland’s O-Line is projected to be one of the worst in the league, and I don’t expect the team to be leading in games for much of the season [[img:quin_02]]. If Judkins can improve his receiving numbers, then there’s hope for him, but for now I’d want someone safer as my RB2. The team doesn’t move me for now, but that could change after a week or two. If there’s one thing that could give me hope for this team’s 2026 campaign, it’s the return of Brandon Aubrey, who is the franchise’s all-time points leader for Kickers and was a part of that great 2024 team [[img:quin_03]]. Let’s see what The Gegwich Effect really looks like. If that easiest projected strength of schedule holds true, then maybe it’ll be a positive effect [[img:quin_04]].

teams.synopsis: When discussing the league’s best WR rooms, I think Cole’s has to be mentioned.
teams.blurb: When discussing the league’s best WR rooms, I think Cole’s has to be mentioned. Puka Nacua is back to practicing, and I’m assuming he’ll be okay suspension-wise, while Ladd McConkey is a “sleeper” WR that many people expect to produce like a WR1 in 2026 with a healthy offensive line and Mike McDaniel coming in as the new offensive coordinator. Then, having Stefon Diggs at the FLEX spot could provide the team with a safe floor week-to-week. However, the RB duo of Jeremiyah Love and TreVeyon Henderson is unproven and questionable, with each one dealing with their own issues, whether that be an ankle injury or competition, respectively. I think the team’s QB and TE will be above league average, so the RB production is the real difference maker between the team once again finishing top 4 in PPG, as they did the past three seasons, and returning to their 2020-2022 form which saw them earn a losing record in each year [[img:cole_01]]. Not to mention, Cole is projected to have the 3rd hardest strength of schedule, and although the tool may not be accurate in a few weeks, it would still be hard to overcome yet another season of tough opponent play like Cole did last season [[img:cole_02]].

This looks bad. Andrew is projected to produce the most points in Week 1 due to his all-star WR trio of Justin Jefferson, Tetairoa McMillan, and Davante Adams, but I only have him ranked 7th in these Week 1 rankings [[img:andrew_01]]. I think it’s simply my bias because Andrew and I drafted at the turn together, so a couple of times he took players that I passed on because I’m not high on them this season, like Tetairoa McMillan and De’Von Achane. However, I can see this team being the one to earn Andrew an over .500 record for the first time since his 2022 season [[img:andrew_02]]. I like the possibility of a Justin Jefferson bounce-back and rotating Baker Mayfield and Patrick Mahomes at QB, depending on the hot hand/better matchup. But I have my reservations about Davante Adams repeating his historical TD efficiency from last season, the 3rd most receiving TDs from any WR since 2021 despite having significantly fewer targets than the other top guys, and De’Von Achane having yet another RB1 year but this time behind a bottom five O-Line and one of the most unknown and unproven offenses we’ve seen in a long time [[img:andrew_03]]. I understand I could be too negative, and those players don’t need to repeat their top seasons to return value, but there’s not enough for me to be confident with to rank the team any higher than this.

teams.synopsis: Despite being projected to score middle-of-the-pack numbers in Week 1, I have Max as a top team in the power rankings ahead of Week 1.
teams.blurb: Despite being projected to score middle-of-the-pack numbers in Week 1, I have Max as a top team in the power rankings ahead of Week 1. So far, MarShawn Lloyd looks like the best pick from the draft with the recent Josh Jacobs news, but we’ll have to wait before we see some production to make any crazy claims. I mentioned Carmine and Ethan as having some of the best RB duos in the league, but Saquon Barkley and Derrick Henry are giving them a run for their money. Those two are actually two of the top three highest scorers in franchise history for Max, with Josh Allen being the other of the top three, so some might call this season a homecoming [[img:max_01]]. The WR duo of Tee Higgins and Marvin Harrison Jr. could definitely be better, but having the Colston Loveland and Caleb Williams stack makes up for it. I think that stack may go crazy this season with both finishing top three at their respective positions. The trio of rookie WRs on the bench also provides some hope for this team’s FLEX if Lloyd, Matthew Golden, or Dallas Goedert don’t end up being viable at that spot. Max “reached” the most on average for his guys out of all managers, although I suspect that number may be inflated by his Cyrus Allen pick. Still, this makes me think that, like Brandon, this is a manager that has done his research and is confident with his roster for 2026 [[img:max_02]]. Last season was the worst in team history, with the team failing to hit the 100 PPG mark for the first time ever, but as this ranking shows, I think the team returns to the best version of itself [[img:max_03]]. Max also leads the league in Missed Wins and Missed Wins Percentage all-time, although that stat is largely driven by his 2024 and 2025 seasons, so I expect him to have better lineup efficiency metrics in 2026 if the team wishes to make its first championship run [[img:max_04]].

teams.synopsis: I think it’s safe to say Baylen shocked ALL of us when he took Tyler Warren in round 4 after taking Brock Bowers in round 2.
teams.blurb: I think it’s safe to say Baylen shocked ALL of us when he took Tyler Warren in round 4 after taking Brock Bowers in round 2. We’ll have to see if that double TE strategy works out, but as of right now I think he would have been better off just taking an RB2, like Jadarian Price or Bhayshul Tuten. Nevertheless, the WR core of Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Luther Burden III has the potential to be one of the best in the league, although it comes at the expense of his RB2 being Tony Pollard and his QB room being unappealing to start the year. The team also has the projected 2nd hardest strength of schedule in the entire league, which is calculated simply from ESPN projections with some data engineering to account for BYE weeks, so it’s a shaky tool but can give us a sense of which teams may have a harder time scoring enough to win games [[img:baylen_01]]. Across league history, Baylen has been a much better waiver/free agent manager, trader, and lineup decision maker than a drafter, so even if it looks shaky now I think in due time he’ll be right back to the upper half of these rankings [[img:baylen_02]].

teams.synopsis: RPM slots into the 10th spot in the initial 2026 rankings, with a roster that I would classify best as fun.
teams.blurb: RPM slots into the 10th spot in the initial 2026 rankings, with a roster that I would classify best as fun. On one hand, there are question marks surrounding Christian McCaffrey’s health for this season after having over 400 touches in 2025 and being in his 30’s, George Kittle’s recovery from his torn Achilles last season, and also Emeka Egbuka’s toe injury, which leaves his Week 1 availability up in the air. However, if all three of those players return to their best version of themselves or even 85% of that, then this team will have a great season. You can even continue that conversation with the wildcards of Jadarian Price as the RB1 for Seattle, Garrett Wilson with hopefully the best offense of his career, and Brian Thomas Jr.’s rookie and sophomore campaigns being opposite sides of the spectrum. Ryan McQuaid’s best season from a PPG perspective was his 2022 season with 110.2 PPG, which is 46th out of 85 teams since 2020 [[img:ryan_01]]. Coinciding with that middling performance, while he’s made the playoffs each of the last four seasons, he has had the luckiest schedule, leading the league in wins over expected since 2020 [[img:ryan_02]]. Ryan is projected to have the 2nd easiest Week 1 matchup, and the 4th easiest strength of schedule, though that will shift as the season gets going [[img:ryan_03]]. Could this year’s squad finally break through to be McQuaid’s best and earn him respect from his peers?

teams.synopsis: The defending champion and only manager with multiple rings enters the 2026 season as the 12th-ranked team on my initial power rankings.
teams.blurb: The defending champion and only manager with multiple rings enters the 2026 season as the 12th-ranked team on my initial power rankings. Being ranked this low is nothing new for Anthony, as he did not crack the top 8 until Week 6 in 2025 and Week 8 in 2022, his two championship-run seasons, so don’t be discouraged by this ranking. The team is projected to be the 2nd lowest-scoring squad in Week 1, right there with Deniz, who won’t have his RB1 [[img:anthony_01]]. This is the cost you pay when you pay up for Josh Allen, who has been a top 2 QB every year since the Preach league’s conception, but Anthony taking him is an outlier when looking at his history of drafting QBs, he has the 2nd highest patience out of all managers all-time [[img:anthony_02]]. Anthony’s RB room is safe; that’s about the best way to describe James Cook III and D’Andre Swift, while his WRs and TE are questionable even for a 14-man league. Additionally, Jordyn Tyson and Zach Charbonnet are both out to start the season, so the team will be limited depth-wise in case his team starts the season slow. Which would not be good, given that this team has the hardest projected strength of schedule as of right now [[img:anthony_03]]. Will he repeat in 2026 or is this going to be a down year for Rolls With Butter?

matchup_of_the_week.blurb: The first Matchup of the Week for 2026 is between our 2nd place team from 2025 and our last place team from 2025, but more importantly, the 1st and 4th ranked teams in the Week 1 power rankings. Charlie is projected to win by 0.9 points, so we really don’t have a clear edge in this matchup. Aidan has beaten Charlie 5-2 all-time, but those two Charlie wins come from two out of the last three meetings. I expect this to be a good matchup, as both teams have similar roster construction, but which top 3 pick will lead their team to a Week 1 win?
